definitions.gloss: Lunar New Year, Chinese New Year
definitions.explanation: The New Year as observed in the traditional lunisolar calendar, falling in late January or February. Widely celebrated in China, Korea, Vietnam, and other Asian countries. In Japan, it is observed in some regions such as Okinawa and by Chinese communities.

examples.japanese: {旧正月|きゅうしょうがつ}は{二月|にがつ}ごろだ。
examples.english: Lunar New Year falls around February.

examples.japanese: {中国|ちゅうごく}では{旧正月|きゅうしょうがつ}が{一年|いちねん}で{最|もっと}も{大|おお}きな{祝日|しゅくじつ}だ。
examples.english: In China, Lunar New Year is the biggest holiday of the year.

examples.japanese: {旧正月|きゅうしょうがつ}の{時期|じき}になると、{多|おお}くの{観光客|かんこうきゃく}がアジア{各地|かくち}から{日本|にほん}を{訪|おとず}れる。
examples.english: When the Lunar New Year period arrives, many tourists from across Asia visit Japan.

notes:
CULTURE:
Japan switched from the lunisolar calendar to the Gregorian calendar in 1873, and most of the country now celebrates {正月|しょうがつ} (New Year) on January 1. However, {旧正月|きゅうしょうがつ} is still recognized in some areas, particularly {沖縄|おきなわ} and in {中華街|ちゅうかがい} (Chinatown) areas like Yokohama and Kobe.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旧正月|きゅうしょうがつ}を{祝|いわ}う: to celebrate Lunar New Year
- {旧正月|きゅうしょうがつ}の{時期|じき}: the Lunar New Year period
- {旧正月|きゅうしょうがつ}{休|やす}み: Lunar New Year holiday

ETYMOLOGY:
{旧|きゅう} (old, former) + {正月|しょうがつ} (New Year) — literally "old New Year," referring to the New Year of the old (pre-Gregorian) calendar.
